translationRepairs: As the Record puts it, "The Three Excellencies are not fixed offices" - meaning the rank exists only when a person worthy of it appears. Shun serving Yao, yiyin day serving Tang, and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao under Zhou are classic examples.

As the Record puts it, "The Three Excellencies are not fixed offices" - meaning the rank exists only when a person worthy of it appears. Shun serving Yao, Yi Yin serving Tang, and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao under Zhou are classic examples.
The Chinese names 伊尹 beside 湯, parallel to 舜之於堯 and 周公、召公於周; 伊尹 is the Shang minister Yi Yin, not a sexagenary day, so "yiyin day" is a garble and Yi Yin is the correct repair.

The Record says, "The Three Excellencies have no fixed office," meaning that only when there are the right men are those posts filled: Shun under Yao, yiyin day under Tang, and the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao under Zhou are examples.

The literal field repeats the same garble; 伊尹於湯 requires Yi Yin under Tang, matching 舜之於堯.
